sentences.show: This spacecraft found an ocean on a moon of Saturn, then destroyed itself to protect it.
Cassini launched on this day in 1997.
It ran on plutonium, because out at Saturn, sunlight is too weak for solar panels.
Seven years later, it reached Saturn.
It dropped a probe onto the moon Titan — the farthest landing ever made.
Then it found geysers of ice, shooting from a tiny moon called Enceladus.
Beneath the ice: a salty ocean, one of the likeliest places to find alien life.
In 2013, it turned to photograph Earth, and asked us to look up and smile.
We were a single dot of light.
But soon it could no longer be steered, and a crash could carry Earth microbes to those moons.
So in 2017, Cassini dived into Saturn — on purpose.
It burned up about 45 seconds after its last signal.
Also on this day: Napoleon's exile on Saint Helena began, and the From Hell letter arrived.
Our app is still in orbit, but it's coming in to land. Subscribe, and be there for the signal.
